evals.prompt: Integrate UI5 Web Components into this webforJ 26.00 app. Upgrade it to the first bundler-capable stable line (26.01 or newer), then create a reusable typed `Ui5Input` Java component for `ui5-input`, load only the required npm module, expose placeholder, value, disabled, and the component's change event, and add a small routed demo view. The frontend bundler must be the default path; do not copy package files into static resources.
evals.expected_output: A webforJ 26.01+ bundler integration using the webforJ build plugin, @BundlePackage/@BundleEntry, and an ElementComposite wrapper with verified properties and event payload.
expectations: LOAD-BEARING: The Maven build config adds/configures the current `com.webforj:webforj-maven-plugin`; Java compilation alone is not treated as sufficient for an npm bundle.
Updates the webforJ version from 26.00 to 26.01 or newer because bundler annotations are unavailable before 26.01.
Uses imports `com.webforj.bundle.annotation.BundlePackage` and `com.webforj.bundle.annotation.BundleEntry`.
Declares `@BundlePackage` for `@ui5/webcomponents` with an explicit npm version range and a narrow `@BundleEntry` for the UI5 Input module rather than importing the whole library.
Creates a reusable class annotated `@NodeName("ui5-input")` that extends `ElementComposite` (not `Component`, `DwcComponent`, or a built-in component).
Models `value`, `placeholder`, and `disabled` with verified property/attribute semantics and fluent Java setters; boolean accessors use a natural `isDisabled` form.
Bridges the real UI5 change/input event to a typed Java event or a correctly configured listener payload without inventing `event.detail.value` if the value actually lives on the host element.
Adds a routed demo that instantiates the wrapper and visibly reacts to the event.
Does NOT copy `node_modules` or UI5 distribution files into `src/main/resources/static`, use a CDN, or add a separate npm build script.

evals.prompt: Add a reusable Chart.js component to this webforJ 26.00 app. Upgrade it to 26.01 or newer and use the frontend bundler as the default integration path. Chart.js is a normal JavaScript library, not a Web Component. I need a Java `Chart` API that accepts typed chart configuration, can update and resize, emits a point-click event with dataset/index values, and cleans up correctly when removed.
evals.expected_output: A TypeScript custom-element adapter under src/main/frontend that owns Chart.js lifecycle, bundled through @BundlePackage/@BundleEntry and exposed through an ElementComposite Java wrapper.
expectations: Uses the webforJ 26.01+ bundler and declares Chart.js through `@BundlePackage` instead of downloading or CDN-loading it.
Updates the webforJ version from 26.00 to 26.01 or newer before introducing bundler APIs.
Creates an authored frontend entry under `src/main/frontend` and binds it with `@BundleEntry`.
The frontend entry registers a hyphenated custom element and imports Chart.js from npm.
The custom element guards duplicate initialization, supports configuration set before connection, and calls Chart.js `destroy()` during disconnect/recreation.
The Java wrapper's `@NodeName` exactly matches the registered custom-element tag and extends `ElementComposite`.
Chart configuration is represented with typed Java model classes/records rather than `Map<String, Object>` as the public API.
Update/resize behavior uses custom-element methods called with `callJsFunctionAsync`/`callJsFunctionVoidAsync`, not user-data string interpolation in `executeJs`.
Point-click is dispatched from the adapter with a minimal serializable payload and bridged to a typed Java event exposing dataset and point indexes.
The normal package/build phase succeeds or the output clearly identifies any external dependency resolution blocker.

evals.prompt: Build a reusable `CustomerSearchBox` from existing webforJ components: a text field, search button, clear button, and a status area. It should expose a small Java API and a search event, but it must not use custom JavaScript or frontend packages.
evals.expected_output: A focused Composite that encapsulates built-in webforJ components and exposes domain methods/events without introducing bundler or ElementComposite machinery.
expectations: Implements the component with `Composite` and a suitable bound webforJ layout.
Does NOT extend `Component`, `DwcComponent`, `TextField`, `Button`, or another built-in component.
Keeps the internal text field, buttons, and status component private and exposes a small domain-oriented fluent API.
Provides a removable Java-side search listener/event and includes the current query in the event without a browser round trip.
Configures normal children/layout/listeners in the constructor rather than using lifecycle hooks unnecessarily.
Does NOT add `@BundleEntry`, `@BundlePackage`, `@JavaScript`, npm files, or frontend source files.
Adds targeted tests for the public API and listener registration.

evals.prompt: This project is staying on webforJ 25.x. Wrap the existing third-party custom element file `src/main/resources/static/vendor/acme-toggle/acme-toggle.js` as a reusable Java component. The element tag is `acme-toggle`, exposes boolean `checked` and `disabled` properties, and emits `toggle-change` with `{ checked }` in `event.detail`. Do not upgrade the framework.
evals.expected_output: A version-aware ElementComposite wrapper using @JavaScript with ws:// and type=module, with no 26.01 bundler APIs.
expectations: Recognizes that webforJ 25.x predates the 26.01 frontend bundler and does NOT use `@BundleEntry`, `@BundlePackage`, or the new build plugin.
Loads the existing file with `@JavaScript` using a correct `ws://vendor/acme-toggle/acme-toggle.js` path and `type="module"`.
Creates `@NodeName("acme-toggle")` wrapper extending `ElementComposite`.
Uses boolean PropertyDescriptors with fluent setters and `isChecked`/`isDisabled` getters.
Creates a typed event for `toggle-change` and extracts `event.detail.checked` without broad fallback expressions.
Does NOT copy, rewrite, or CDN-replace the provided third-party file.
Adds targeted PropertyDescriptor/listener tests compatible with the project's existing test setup.

evals.prompt: Add a reusable `MapView` component to this webforJ 26.00 app backed by the Leaflet npm package. Upgrade it to 26.01 or newer and use the frontend bundler. I need a Java API for center coordinates and zoom, and a marker-click event. Leaflet also ships its own stylesheet that must load with the component.
evals.expected_output: A bundler integration that works around Leaflet being an unscoped npm package: a local frontend entry importing leaflet and its CSS, bound with @BundleEntry, plus an ElementComposite wrapper.
expectations: LOAD-BEARING: Does NOT write `@BundleEntry("leaflet/dist/leaflet.js")` or any other unscoped npm module path, because only `@scope`-prefixed values are treated as npm specifiers and an unscoped one is silently dropped from the build.
Declares `@BundlePackage(value = "leaflet", version = ...)` with an explicit semver range.
Authors a local entry under `src/main/frontend` that imports `leaflet` and imports `leaflet/dist/leaflet.css` for its side effect, and binds that file with `@BundleEntry`.
Updates the webforJ version from 26.00 to 26.01 or newer and adds/configures `com.webforj:webforj-maven-plugin` with `<extensions>true</extensions>`.
The entry registers a hyphenated custom element that creates the Leaflet map in `connectedCallback`, guards duplicate initialization, and calls Leaflet `remove()` on disconnect.
The Java wrapper extends `ElementComposite` with a matching `@NodeName`, exposes typed center/zoom setters, and bridges marker click to a typed event with a minimal payload.
Does NOT add a CDN link, copy Leaflet files into `src/main/resources/static`, or use `@StyleSheet` for the Leaflet CSS.
Verification runs the package/build phase rather than treating `mvn compile` as sufficient.

evals.prompt: In this webforJ 26.00 app, build a reusable `PriceTag` component as a Lit element, and style it with SCSS that uses variables from a shared partial living in a `styles` folder. Upgrade the project as needed. The component takes an amount and a currency and emits a click event carrying the amount.
evals.expected_output: A Lit entry plus a SCSS entry bound to the wrapper class, with the SCSS load path configured in bun.config.ts, and no manually enabled SCSS extension.
expectations: Updates webforJ from 26.00 to 26.01 or newer and adds the webforJ build plugin.
Declares `@BundlePackage` for `lit` and authors the element under `src/main/frontend`, bound with `@BundleEntry`.
Does NOT enable the SCSS extension by id or add `sass` as a `@BundlePackage`; the extension activates automatically because a `.scss` source is present and declares `sass` itself.
Sets the SCSS load path in `src/main/frontend/bun.config.ts` under the `webforj-scss` key so the shared partial resolves, rather than using relative `../..` paths or duplicating the partial.
Binds the annotations to the reusable `PriceTag` class itself, not to a demo view, so the component carries its frontend wherever it is used.
Uses `PropertyDescriptor` for amount and currency with fluent, validated Java setters.
Bridges the click to a typed `ComponentEvent` extracting the amount from the event detail without a broad fallback expression that would discard a zero amount.
Does NOT author anything under `src/main/frontend/generated`, and does not commit `node_modules`.
